decisions.reason: As a newly launched core safety-shoe line, it fits the firm's main business and recent investment makes management likely to give it more time rather than withdraw it quickly.

The comfort insole is a complementary product with lower public prominence, but the firm is still likely to retain it because it supports its footwear system offering and any weak early uptake can be seen as temporary.
The supportive insole is somewhat easier to discontinue than a flagship shoe line, yet recent development effort and its role in tailored solutions make continued commitment more likely than exit.
The ergonomic safety shoe series has strong public commitment through its own page and is closely aligned with the firm's innovation direction, so escalation of commitment strongly favors keeping it.
Firefighter and rescue boots serve a more specialized segment, but they remain within the firm's protective-footwear competence and management would likely justify staying the course after launch.
Being shown on the home page signals visible commitment, and as a complementary innovation tied to the core shoe business the moulded insole is likely to be kept on the market.
